summary: On-demand SIEM export including credential-rotation events and session-context correlation for audit
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requested a one-off SIEM export that must include: (1) all credential lifecycle events (create, rotate, revoke), (2) session context (session_id, user_agent, source_ip) correlated to each event, and (3) per-batch signed manifests for audit. Purpose: external audit for access control and key rotation.

Impact:
- Audit team at MonetaBank cannot complete evidence pack for a regulatory review unless rotation events are demonstrably present and tied to session context.
- Customer considers this a blocking compliance deliverable (internal deadline 2026-03-15).

Requested deliverables:
- NDJSON sample with credential.rotation, credential.create, credential.revoke event types for a 7-day window (2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09).
- Mapping document: Redwood audit fields -> MonetaBank SIEM fields (session_id, subject_id, request_id, ip, user_agent).
- Signed manifest (RFC3161-style timestamp) per export batch.

Notes: Customer explicitly requested that any PII be redacted except unique subject identifiers accepted by their legal team. They want the export delivered to an S3 bucket with presigned URL and a delivery confirmation in the ticket.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs a set of actions that trigger credential rotation in prod (service account rotate via console or API)
2) Verify events appear in internal audit stream: event_type in [credential.*]
3) Trigger export job (support-managed) via audit-exporter job with passthrough filters for event_type and time window
4) Validate NDJSON contains session_id and ip fields correlated to each rotation event
5) Verify per-batch manifest and the signature header

Observed behavior seen by customer: rotation events present in console UI but not surfaced in the exported NDJSON sample they received from a prior run (missing event_type credential.rotation; session context fields blank).
logs:
Sample redacted entries from internal stream (prod):
2026-03-05T14:22:11Z | event_type: credential.rotate | subject_id: svc-billing-42 | session_id: sess-7f2b | ip: 198.51.100.23 | user_agent: Redwood/CLI-v1.9
2026-03-05T14:22:12Z | event_type: auth.session.start | subject_id: svc-billing-42 | session_id: sess-7f2b | ip: 198.51.100.23
2026-03-06T03:08:09Z | event_type: credential.revoke | subject_id: user-jdoe | session_id: sess-88a2 | ip: 203.0.113.9

Exporter trace (support-run): audit-exporter v2.6.1 started export job id=exp-20260310-81; applied filters: event_type in [credential.create,credential.rotate,credential.revoke], time_window=2026-03-02T00:00Z..2026-03-09T23:59Z; output=ndjson.gz to s3://redwood-support-deliveries/monetabank/exp-20260310-81.ndjson.gz

Problem observed in prior run: exported NDJSON missing any event where event_type contained '.' (dot) due to a downstream field-flattening step in the pipeline.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Aisha): confirmed customer saw rotation events in Console and in raw Kafka topic (audit.activity). Support attempted a manual run of audit-exporter and observed missing event_type when pipeline stage 'field-flatten' ran (it stripped dotted keys incorrectly).

SRE follow-up (Diego): reproduced locally with audit-exporter v2.6.1 by replaying sample topic. Confirmed: flattening lambda (json-flatten-service v1.3) converts 'credential.rotate' key to nested structure and the exporter filters by flat string 'credential.rotate' which fails the match. Root cause: field-normalizer config omitted preserve_dotted_keys=true for exports with event_type pattern matching.

Mitigation performed: updated json-flatten-service config to preserve dotted keys for export queues (preserve_dotted_keys=true) and patched audit-exporter to normalize event_type by reading raw 'event_type' string before flattening (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4871). Added unit tests to cover dotted event_type values.

QA: re-ran export job exp-20260312-01, verified NDJSON contains three credential.rotate entries and session_id populated. Signed manifest generated by manifest-signer v1.1 with RFC3161 timestamp and S3 object checksum.

2026-03-12 15:55 - MonetaBank (Security contact - Elena Rossi): Confirmed receipt of sample NDJSON and per-batch manifest. Asked for delivery to their S3 bucket and the signed manifest in PKCS7 form.

Support response: scheduled final delivery and produced PKCS7 envelope via manifest-signer v1.1. Delivery completed 2026-03-12 18:10 UTC.
resolution_notes:
Root cause: field-flatten stage dropped dotted event_type keys leading to exporter filter mismatch. Fix: enable preserve_dotted_keys in json-flatten-service and modify audit-exporter to read raw event_type prior to flattening.

Deliverables provided to customer (MonetaBank):
- NDJSON export (7-day window) placed at s3://monetabank-evidence/exports/exp-20260312-01.ndjson.gz
- PKCS7-signed per-batch manifest: s3://monetabank-evidence/exports/exp-20260312-01.manifest.p7s
- Field mapping document (Redwood -> MonetaBank) attached as mapping_moneta_20260312.csv
- Post-deploy validation screenshots and Kibana query links included in support attachment.

Ticket resolved after customer confirmation 2026-03-12 18:25 UTC.
